sense: bring out something new: a product, a book, a show

terms.gloss: bring out, publish; put on (a show)
evidence: Cic. Brut. 19: dē rē pūblicā librōs ēdidistī
Lewis & Short: lūdōs ēdere, to put on games
terms.comment: To give out, put forth (Lewis & Short): of a book, to publish it; of games or a show, to put it on. Not edō, edere, to eat, with a short e. To launch a campaign or a big undertaking is to begin it, incohāre (see begin).

terms.gloss: put on the market (a new product)
terms.grammar: verb phrase: prōdūcō, prōdūcere, prōdūxī, prōductum
evidence: M-O s.v. market: put on the market, after Egger
Ter. Eun. 1.2.54 (old numbering): ancillam prōdūxit, vēndidit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically prōdūcere is to bring out for sale, of slaves in Terence (Lewis & Short); Egger adds vēnāle, for sale.

phrases.latin: nam ut illōs dē rē pūblicā librōs ēdidistī, nihil ā tē sānē posteā accēpimus
phrases.english: for since you brought out those books on the State, we have had nothing at all from you

sources: Lewis & Short: edo · Lewis & Short: produco
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. market.
